correctness.rationale: A complete analytic proof establishes the row norm A+t−2min(a_n,t), the operator norm A+t, and the t/2 monomorphism estimate. Norm attainment forces finite support by equality in a summable weighted triangle inequality; a matching finite-support witness exists. Weak-star closure equals the weak-star continuous image of Bℓ∞ by finite truncations and compactness. A zero coefficient constructs an exact weak-star norm-maximizer; full positive support excludes every such maximizer via coordinatewise strictness and phase rigidity. Explicit normalized approximations establish all three strata norm dense at mass A; the full-support stratum is residual while its dense complement is meager, and the distance of the operators is exactly the coefficient ℓ1 distance. Real and complex scalar cases and positive endpoints were checked.

value.rationale: The theorem exhausts three distinct norm-attainment levels along an isometrically parameterized, natural rank-one perturbation family of a canonical Banach-space inclusion. It proves all three strata dense even with exactly the same operator norm, yet weak-star quasi norm attainment is meager and its failure residual in that same simplex; this sharp generic-failure instability is not supplied by a mere approximation theorem. Full support produces an explicit nonremotal weak-star compact convex image. The support boundary, fixed-norm instability and generic-failure dichotomy are mathematically motivated by the 2022 weak-star quasi attainment theory and not an arbitrary numerical slice.
